scenario: AITA For telling my Girlfriend she needs to quit whining about who eats what or I'll kick her out | Well, the title says it all, the past few weeks have both been really great and extremely infuriating. We don't live together, but we decided it would be best to stick together during these times as we have no family near as such she is staying with me as I have my own apartment and she has multiple roommates hence the choice. Well she eats more then any person I have ever known, especially considering her physical appearance, she is 5'4, petite, thin and yet she eats more than I do and I am 6'6 and a bit of a gymbro. To put it in to perspective, our food bill each week is roughly three times compared to what I usually spend alone. Yet she seems extremely selfconcious about this and as a result will act surprised when something is gone, try to blame me, states I am eating too much whenever I eat anything, essentially, she tries to deflect her eating habits and projects them on to me out of embarrassment about her eating so much I guess? The thing is, I don't care about her eating habits, she can eat whatever she wants to eat what I am done with is her constantly trying to blame me, whining about food and picking fights about it. I talked to her about it multiple times, argued with her about it multiple times but earlier today I just got so tired of another comment, this time brought on by me making a sandwhich at 2 PM when I had eaten at 10 AM I know right, horrible. So I told her that this crap was either going to stop right here and now or I'll kick her out and she can spend the coming weeks or months at her own place. She just started crying, called me horrible and locked herself in the bathroom. At this point I just dont get it anymore, am I being TA here or is she TA?

By following this plan, you can efficiently prepare for Diwali, ensuring a clean, decorated, and welcoming home for your relatives.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the guy in this situation is being "AITA" (Am I The Asshole) or not. Let me start by understanding the scenario. He's living with his girlfriend in his apartment because she has multiple roommates and no family nearby. They've been together for a few weeks, and it's been both great and infuriating. The main issue seems to be about food. She eats a lot more than him, even though she's petite and thin, while he's 6'6 and a gym enthusiast. Their weekly food bill is triple what he used to spend alone. She's self-conscious about her eating habits, so she acts surprised when food is gone, blames him, and accuses him of eating too much. He's tired of her whining and deflecting, so he told her to stop or he'll kick her out. She cried and locked herself in the bathroom. Now, the question is: Is he being the asshole here, or is she? First, I need to consider both perspectives. On one hand, he's footing the bill for the groceries, and her eating habits are significantly increasing the expenses. It's understandable that he'd be frustrated, especially since she's not taking responsibility for her actions but instead blaming him. He's tried talking to her multiple times, but it hasn't helped, so he snapped and threatened to kick her out. On the other hand, she's in a stressful situation, living with someone she's not used to, and dealing with her own self-consciousness about her eating habits. It's possible that she's feeling insecure or embarrassed, which leads to her defensive behavior. Threatening to kick her out might have been an overreaction, especially if they're not living together permanently and she has other options. I also need to think about the communication style. He's tried talking to her, but it seems like they've had multiple arguments without resolution. Maybe a different approach to communication could have been more effective. Instead of threatening, he could have suggested ways to manage the food expenses together or found a compromise. Another angle is the financial aspect. If he's paying for groceries, it's reasonable for him to expect some consideration regarding expenses. However, everyone has different eating habits, and it's not fair to single someone out without understanding their feelings or circumstances. In conclusion, while his frustration is understandable, the way he handled the situation by threatening to kick her out might be seen as being the asshole. A more empathetic and collaborative approach could have been more effective in resolving the issue.
